title: OpenAPI compliance: documentation gaps across the spec (descriptions, parameter docs, operationId)
description:
## Overview

A compliance matrix over our API definitions identified gaps in the documentation features clients rely on. Still no urgency — this remains a reminder ticket, best addressed per-API as each is touched.

## Which standard

The original analysis was run against **OpenAPI 3.2.0**, and that is now the current released specification (Sept 2025) — the links below point at it. We publish `openapi: 3.1.0` today. The distinction does not affect this ticket: `summary`, `description`, `operationId` and the Schema Object are documentation fields whose meaning is unchanged between the two versions, and 3.2 is a non-breaking feature release over 3.1.

**Repo policy, landed 2026-07-10:** CLAUDE.md now carries a MUST rule — *the OpenAPI spec is the contract, never a validator's defaults* — and states the version stance explicitly: **cite 3.2, emit 3.1**, until Akto is proven against 3.2. The QA cheat sheet's spec pill reads `OpenAPI 3.1 (3.2 target)`. No emitted artefact changed: `secuura-api.yaml` still declares `3.1.0` and the generator still constructs `OpenApiGeneratorV31`.

Adopting 3.2 is a separate piece of work with its own blocker — [KS-429](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-429/openapi-32-readiness-akto-cannot-parse-32-swagger-parser-2248-sequence). In short: Akto parses specs with Java `swagger-parser`, whose 3.2 support ([swagger-api/swagger-parser#2248](<https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-parser/issues/2248>)) is still open with no activity, so a 3.2 document would be rejected outright at import and every Akto scan would run against an empty collection. **Any spec-version bump needs testing against Akto first.** Nothing in this ticket requires it — every item below is valid under both versions.

* [OpenAPI 3.2.0](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0>) — [Operation Object](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0#operation-object>) (`summary`, `description`, `operationId`) · [Parameter Object](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0#parameter-object>) (`description`) · [Schema Object](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0#schema-object>)

*(Attached file autogenerated from the* `api-explorer` *code.)*

## Current state — re-measured 2026-07-10

Counted directly from the published spec: **316 operations** across **284 paths**, with **183 declared parameters**.

| Feature | Missing | Coverage | Since original |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `operationId` | **316 / 316** | 100% missing | *not previously measured* |
| Parameter `description` | **183 / 183** | 100% missing | (was 140 endpoints) |
| Operation `description` | 225 / 316 | 71.2% missing | improved (was 250) |
| 2xx response schema | 8 / 316 | 2.5% missing | improved (was 10) |
| Request body schema | 0 / 128 | ✅ complete | **resolved** (was 42) |
| 4xx/5xx error response | 0 / 316 | ✅ complete | **resolved** (was 1) |
| Operation `summary` | 0 / 316 | ✅ complete | — |

Two of the original six gaps have closed entirely, and two others narrowed — good progress from work done in the meantime. The remaining picture is dominated by three items.

## What stands out now

`operationId` **— 0 of 316.** Not measured in the original pass, and the most consequential omission. Per the [Operation Object](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0#operation-object>) it is optional, but it is the handle that tooling keys on: `openapi-generator` derives client method names from it, and OpenAPI `links` **must** reference an operation by `operationId`. Its absence is a hard blocker for [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) (stateful POST→GET→DELETE chains) — you cannot declare a link to an operation that has no id. Worth doing first for that reason alone.

**Parameter descriptions — 183 of 183.** Every declared parameter lacks a `description`. Cheap to add where the source `*.openapi.ts` registration already knows what the parameter means, and it is the field a developer reads in Swagger UI before anything else.

**Operation descriptions — 225 of 316.** All 316 have a `summary`, so nothing is anonymous; the gap is the longer-form explanation. Lower priority than the two above.

## Suggested sequencing

1. `operationId` **on every operation** — mechanical, unblocks [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete)'s `links` work, and improves generated clients immediately.
2. **Parameter** `description`**s** — 183 fields, most one line each.
3. **Operation** `description`**s** — incrementally, as each API is touched.
4. **The 8 operations missing a 2xx response schema** — small, and each is likely a deliberate no-content response worth confirming rather than assuming.

Note that `secuura-api.yaml` is **generated** and byte-compared by `npm run check:openapi`, so all of the above are edits to the per-service `*.openapi.ts` registrations, followed by `npm run generate-openapi`. All four items emit constructs valid under 3.1 as well as 3.2, so none of them wait on [KS-429](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-429/openapi-32-readiness-akto-cannot-parse-32-swagger-parser-2248-sequence).

Each API can be updated independently, so there is flexibility in scheduling. Happy to help with any of it — particularly step 1, which is the one with a downstream dependency.

## Related

* [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) — stateful `links` + `operationId`. **Depends on step 1 here**; also blocked by [KS-428](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and).
* [KS-429](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-429/openapi-32-readiness-akto-cannot-parse-32-swagger-parser-2248-sequence) — OpenAPI 3.2 readiness; Akto cannot parse 3.2 yet, so the version bump must be tested against it first.
* [KS-424](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-424/openapi-auth-contract-make-security-explicit-on-every-operation) — makes `security` explicit on every operation (a separate Operation Object field with the same "implied vs stated" problem).
* [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) — OpenAPI inline examples; [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) — request schema tightening. Parallel work in the same generated file.

**BLUF:** Kam ruled on 2026-11-10 to demote this ticket from High to Medium. KS-188 carries the operationId step, and this comment moves the priority to Medium.

**What was ruled.** Card `secuura-ks61-openapi-gaps-demote-1109`, option a: "Demote to Medium; KS-188 carries the operationId step".

**The dependency stays on record.** This ticket's own 2026-07-10 re-measure counts operationId missing on 316 of 316 operations and calls it "a hard blocker for KS-188 (stateful POST→GET→DELETE chains)". That has not changed. KS-188 stays High and is where the operationId step is carried.

**What this does not do.** It does not change the assignee, the state, KS-188's priority or this ticket's list of gaps (parameter descriptions 183 of 183, operation descriptions 225 of 316, 8 operations without a 2xx schema). No code changes with this comment.

## Results 2026-09-14 (Schemathesis 4.27.1) — the spec-documentation gaps the sweep can see

From `full-2026-09-14T15-04-07Z-slot3` (342 ops, 0 errored; `develop` @ `64c386e04`), the contract-documentation findings a sweep exposes, for this ticket's per-API-as-touched pass:

* **Undocumented status codes** (`status_code_conformance`): `PATCH /api/did/{did}` ×2, and `POST /api/wallets/verify` answering an undocumented **400** to a malformed body — KS-488 C-2 removed 400 from that operation's spec, but the gateway's JSON-parse 400 still occurs. Either the 400 belongs back in the declared set (it is a gateway behaviour on every JSON operation), or it does not and the gateway should not emit it — KS-627's contract work decides.
* **`unresolvable_reference`** (new warning in 4.26.0, now fatal via `[warnings] fail-on`): fired on **0** operations — no dangling `$ref`s.
* **`links`/`operationId`**: still none declared (KS-188); 4.27.0's dependency inference is now guessing chains the spec does not state.
* **`base_url_mismatch`**: 73 ops — a known false positive for this spec (404-only precondition probes), classified informational under KS-1169.

Nothing here changes this ticket's status; it stays a per-API reminder. Refs as KS-NNN text.

## Link: Schemathesis Stateful Testing (KS-188)

**Related Issue:** KS-188 - Schemathesis: Stateful Testing Configured But Produces Zero Execution Results

This ticket's gaps directly impact KS-188's ability to execute stateful testing:

### Connection

**KS-61 Gaps:**
- Parameter documentation: 55.6% missing (183/329 endpoints)
- Request body schemas: 59.3% missing (195/329 endpoints)

**KS-188 Impact:**
- Stateful testing phase runs but produces zero execution results
- Hypothesis/Schemathesis cannot discover valid operation chains (POST→GET→DELETE)
- Missing `x-links` definitions prevent resource lifecycle linking
- Incomplete schemas prevent payload generation for state-transition chains

### Root Cause Link

Stateful testing requires complete OpenAPI spec metadata:
1. **Full parameter definitions** — to understand what inputs each operation accepts
2. **Complete request/response schemas** — to generate valid payloads and verify state transitions
3. **Operation linking (x-links)** — to define POST→GET→DELETE chains explicitly

The 55.6% missing parameters and 59.3% missing request schemas in KS-61 are likely the reason stateful testing cannot execute.

### Recommendation

Address KS-61 gaps incrementally as `.openapi.ts` files are enhanced:
- Add operation linking via `x-links` definitions
- Complete parameter documentation
- Register all request body schemas with Zod/sharedRegistry

This should unlock stateful testing in KS-188.

## Status Update — Significant Compliance Improvement (2026-06-03)

**Status: IMPROVED** ✅ (from 63.6% → high compliance on core features)

## Root Cause of Improvement: `.openapi.ts` Implementation

**Decision (**[KS-3](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-3/discussion-schemathesis-implementation-readiness-see-ks-50)**, 2026-05-07):** Make `.openapi.ts` the single source of truth for API documentation.

**How it works:**

1. Each service has `services/<svc>/src/<svc>.openapi.ts` with Zod schema definitions
2. `generate-openapi.ts` aggregates all `.openapi.ts` files into `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`
3. Zod schemas automatically provide descriptions, types, and validation rules
4. Response envelopes are auto-documented from shared schema patterns

**Result:**

* ✅ Descriptions now pulled from `.openapi.ts` comments → 100% coverage
* ✅ Response schemas auto-generated from Zod → 100% coverage
* ⚠️ Parameters & request bodies still require explicit Zod schema registration

---

## What's Still Needed

### Parameters (55.6% missing)

**Why:** Some endpoints have dynamic or matrix parameters that need explicit OpenAPI parameter definitions.
**Example:** `GET /api/documents/{id}/verify` needs `{id}` path parameter documented.
**Fix:** Add parameter definitions to Zod schemas or OpenAPI registry in `.openapi.ts` files.

### Request Body Schemas (59.3% missing)

**Why:** Some endpoints (mostly GETs, public endpoints) don't have request bodies, but some POST/PATCH endpoints might need explicit schema registration.
**Fix:** Ensure all request payloads are registered with `sharedRegistry` in `.openapi.ts`.

---

## Affected by Recent Work

[KS-3](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-3/discussion-schemathesis-implementation-readiness-see-ks-50) **(**`.openapi.ts` **single source of truth):** ✅ Directly improved descriptions & responses
[KS-144](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-144/platform-k-triage-and-fix-the-75-genuine-schemathesis-findings-dev-run) **(Triage 75 Schemathesis findings):** ✅ Drove schema alignment (resolved response_schema_conformance issues)
[KS-122](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-122/schemathesis-suite-content-remediation-write-test-role-scope-api-key) **(Suite content remediation):** ✅ Aligned test data to actual API shapes

These tickets collectively improved OpenAPI compliance by enforcing schema consistency.

---

## Recommendation

**Status: LOW PRIORITY** ✅

The critical compliance features (descriptions, responses) are now complete. The remaining gaps (parameters, request bodies) are less critical but still beneficial.

**Next steps (optional, no urgency):**

1. Review `.openapi.ts` files to ensure all parameters are documented
2. Add missing request body schemas via Zod registry
3. Re-run compliance analysis in 1-2 quarters to track progress

**Note:** The original ticket suggested "no urgency" and "address as you go" — that approach is working. Core features are now solid, gaps are minor, and ongoing development will incrementally close them.

---

## Summary

From **63.6% overall completeness** to **descriptions & responses at 100%** — a direct result of implementing `.openapi.ts` as the source of truth. The API is now properly documented where it matters most.
